I woke up at stupid o'clock this morning. Actually, I've woken up at stupid o'clock the last three mornings because I keep forgetting to either reset or turn off my stupid alarm on my stupid phone.

And just why, you might ask, is it set to stupid o'clock? And why, if I didn't want it to be the other two days, was it still set to stupid o'clock?

Valid inquiries, indeed.

On Thursday I had to take Stacy to a second gig at stupid o'clock so I could go get the allergy shots d'mort at not quite stupid o'clock and then pick her back up three hours or so after stupid o'clock so she could take me to work at normal o'clock so she could go back to her second gig then, a couple hours later, come hang in the library as I continued working at whatever o'clock.

And, me being me, I've forgotten to do anything about the alarm for yesterday or this morning.

Any time someone tells you librarians are smarter than your average homo sapiens? Remember the last couple of paragraphs.

Anyway, I was especially sad about it this morning because it interrupted a dream . . . a rather interesting dream . . . a scifi dream . . . crap, once I start using ellipses I just can't seem to stop . . . brace yourself for the rest of this horrific paragraph . . . so I don't often remember my dreams . . . probably because I usually wake up slowly and comfortably at regular o'clock, dontchaknow . . . and frankly dreams kinda piss me off . . . I mean, come on, brain, you have shit to work out while you're busy taking a bath . . view Boston University talking about brain washing during sleep . . . then go ahead and do watcha gotta do but leave me out of it, right, and let me get on with sleeping . . . but I was so excited to have a scifi dream that when the alarm went off at stupid o'clock this morning I was a little sad about it . . . and it was, like Douglas Adams scifi-y, not that boring, like, world-building/what did the space emperor have for breakfast/what exactly are the specs of the roto-explodo-super-electro cannon on the flagship scifi-y . . . and no . . . I'm afraid I don't remember many of the specifics . . . just that it was HHGTTG-ish . . . and that I was having a good time with it.

Where was I going with all this?

Ah yes.

So, stupid o'clock. And just what is stupid o'clock, you might also ask? Well, I'd argue it's pretty subjective, I mean, I could give you an actual time - it was 6am - but that wouldn't tell you that's hours before I usually get up to go to my job that starts at 10am, and, frankly, I'm a little sore at the implication that my stupid o'clock might not be stupid enough for the likes of you. Heck, I bet your version of stupid o'clock is 4am, right? Or 3am? Something far worse than my piddly 6am.

Should "far" in the last paragraph be bolded or italicized? Why do I think it should be italicized? And just why am I leaving it bolded?

To continue.

Pah! I bet you're thinking to yourself. 6am?! I wish 6am would be stupid o'clock! How much better my life would be if such a paltry, sad, time in the am would be a horrible time to wake up! Luxury!

At which point I'd have to start in on the Monty Python bit where-

Sorry . . . sorry . . . I think waking up too early these last couple of days has made me a tad punchy. It may be best if I just wrap up this entry now and go lie down for a nap. I did, after all, wake up at stupid o'clock this morning.

Trees have been around for ~400 million years. There are currently ~3 trillion mature trees on earth. (Thanks, Wikipedia!) Modern humans have been around for hundreds of thousands of years. Primates have been around for millions of years. (Thanks, again, Wikipedia!)

What I'm getting at here is that trees and humans have been around each other for a long time, yeah?

So how is it that my allergies are so bad? How is it possible that millions of years of evolution have produced me, a walking talking ape that is so allergic to trees that I need four - FOUR! - allergy shots a month?

I mean, come on, body. Are you even, like, trying?

The good news? My doc popped into the room today to make sure I, you know, hadn't DIED or anything after having multiple vials of poison shot directly into my body and told me how much she was enjoying View Terry Pratchett's website - Terry Pratchett.

I got my doc hooked on Terry Pratchett books, y'all!

She said she was reading one at home and listening to a second one in her car. She couldn't stop smiling.

Your friendly neighborhood librarian, risking death by anaphylaxis to get the right book in the right hand.

It's been nearly a quarter century since i owned the bakiwop.com domain. Tonight? Tonight I couldn't fall asleep so I went downstairs, fired up the pc, and, for some reason, checked to see if it was available (I'd checked on and off over the years to no avail, natch) . . . and there it was, just waiting for me, looking all pretty and shiny on the domain registrar shelf. How cool is that?
